source.title: Scalable Vision Language Model Training via High Quality Data Curation
source.authors: Hongyuan Dong; Zijian Kang; Weijie Yin; Xiao Liang; Chao Feng; Jiao Ran

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how benchmark performance changes with training-data scale in vision-language pretraining and SFT, extending scaling questions to a different modality and training setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports benchmark-performance curves and correlations, not held-out cross-entropy loss. It does not test parameter-count or compute scaling, compute-optimal allocation, architecture-shape effects, or prediction of much larger runs from small-run loss fits. The ordinary GPT and human evaluation prompts in the appendices are evaluation instructions, not instructions directed at an AI reading or reviewing this paper.
record.test_reason: In a vision-language setting, the study reports how downstream benchmark scores change with training-data size across one 2B model's pretraining and SFT stages. This bears on V6 (downstream performance improves predictably with scale). It measures no held-out loss, no parameter or compute sweep, no compute-optimal split and no architecture-shape comparison, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SAIL-VL-2B's visual-comprehension benchmark scores improve logarithmically with pretraining data size (up to 655B tokens), and that post-SFT scores track this. SAIL-Instruction gives the best SFT data-quantity scaling, and curriculum SFT improves the scaling curve from logarithmic (all-in-one) to near-linear. In the limitations they say the data-size laws cover only one data magnitude and one model size, with saturation observed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses vision-language models and benchmark scores rather than text-model held-out cross-entropy loss; varies training-data size and SFT strategy rather than parameter count or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance curves differ by training stage and SFT strategy: curriculum SFT is near-linear while all-in-one SFT is logarithmic. Pretraining-to-SFT correlations are reported separately for SFT-Instruction and LLaVA-Next SFT data.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretraining visual-understanding benchmark scores strongly predict post-SFT open-source benchmark scores across checkpoints: ρ=0.97, R²=0.94 (SFT-Instruction) and ρ=0.99, R²=0.98 (LLaVA-Next).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Upstream (pretraining-stage) benchmark performance linearly predicts post-fine-tuning downstream performance in VLMs.

record.problems: The scaling analysis is limited to SAIL-VL-2B and a specific data magnitude; the authors note saturation and uncertainty about further gains. The scaling outcomes are primarily presented as plotted curves without exact values in the text. No held-out loss, parameter-count sweep, or compute-optimal allocation is tested.
record.rows_left_out: Benchmark comparisons among final SAIL-VL and other model families in Tables 4, 10, and 11 are not scaling results. Data-quality comparisons and caption evaluations in Tables 1, 5, 6, and 8 and Figures 8–9 do not report the benchmark behavior named by V6 as a function of model scale or pretraining loss.

untested.parts: Scaling with model parameter count or compute (only SAIL-VL-2B is scaled); predictability from pretraining loss; extrapolation beyond the explored data range.
All: no held-out loss is measured.
All: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit in loss for the VLM setting; only benchmark-score trends are reported.
No exponents or fitting choices are compared.

missing.what: Axis ranges for the pretraining and SFT scaling figures, giving the magnitude of the gains. Fig 2: about 45.5–49.5 over log2(M) 2–6. Fig 3(a): 54–62 over log2(M) 3–8. Fig 3(b): 67.4–68.0. Fig 3(c): 57.0–59.0.
Scaling points are checkpoints from a single run at different steps, each given 2M-sample annealing, not independently trained runs. This affects how the data-scale curves should be read.

record.verdict_notes: The 'scaling laws' here are log-linear fits of benchmark scores against data size for a single 2B model. They are not power laws in loss. The 8B model was not part of any scaling sweep.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law loss scaling against parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run loss fits are used to predict losses of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute budget allocation between parameter count and tokens is tested.
The paper does not compare architecture depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns vision-language models and SFT, but measures benchmark performance rather than the claimed power-law form in held-out loss across modalities or training regimes.

Tests benchmark performance against training-data size and correlation between pretraining visual-understanding benchmarks and post-SFT benchmark performance; does not test predictability from held-out pretraining loss or across model parameter counts.

No loss-law exponents or compute-optimal splits are estimated or compared across fitting choices. The paper notes saturation within its explored data magnitude, but does not test whether held-out loss curves bend away from a power law.

rows.subject: SAIL-VL-2B
rows.operation_detail: Trains and evaluates the model on SAIL-Instruction at varying data sizes.
rows.value: Performance scales up stably; SAIL-Instruction has the highest performance at every plotted data point among the compared collections.
rows.note: The paper describes the scale trend and relative ranking; exact plotted scores are not stated in the text.

rows.subject: SAIL-VL-2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluates benchmark performance across the three progressively more complex SFT stages.
rows.value: The curriculum strategy exhibits a near-linear performance scaling curve across training stages.
rows.note: The stages have different data collections and quantities; exact plotted scores are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Confounded. The three curriculum stages differ in data type and complexity as well as cumulative size, so the curve is not a clean data-scale effect.

rows.subject: SAIL-VL-2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluates benchmark performance with all three SFT-stage data collections combined in a single training loop.
rows.value: The AIO strategy exhibits a logarithmic performance scaling curve.
rows.note: The authors report the curve as less favorable than the curriculum strategy; exact plotted scores are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Should be observed, not partial. 'Logarithmic' on Figure 5's linear size axis is the same log-linear growth the paper reports for pretraining. AIO still improves steadily (7M→36.5M); it is only lower than curriculum SFT. It is also a strategy comparison, not a weaker scaling effect.

relationships.condition: SAIL-VL-2B, benchmark score vs training-data size in pretrain-alignment, pretrain-advance, post-SFT and SFT data-quantity experiments
relationships.reason: Scores rise roughly linearly in log data size across stages and SFT datasets (r1–r7, r9). The curriculum stages (r8) are confounded by data type.
relationships.display_finding: Scores increased roughly linearly with log data size across training stages and SFT datasets, although curriculum comparisons also changed data type.

relationships.condition: Post-SFT scores, and the upper end of the explored pretraining data range
relationships.reason: Post-SFT gains are under one point on SAIL-Instruction across a 32x pretraining-data increase (r5, axis 67.4–68.0). The authors also say performance is saturating at this data quantity (r12).
relationships.display_finding: A 32-fold pretraining-data increase yielded less than one point on SAIL-Instruction after supervised fine-tuning, with performance saturating at the explored data scale.
